rule_level_problems.problem: 'Feeling physically tense' stands in for the page's observed sign 'tense posturing like gripping arm rails tightly, clenching fists'. It is a subjective feeling (parent 'Feeling tense'), not an observed behaviour. 'Muscle tension' (finding) or 'Physically threatening behavior' (finding) would be closer; neither is exact.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: aggressive/disruptive patient with signs of escalating aggression
rule_level_problems.problem: Five of the ten red-box concepts (Anger reaction, Provocative behavior, Verbal aggression, Physical aggression, Destructive behavior) are SNOMED descendants of 'Aggressive behavior', so recording any one of them alone satisfies both arms of the (and ...). The other five (Challenging behavior, Verbally abusive behavior, Feeling physically tense, Restlessness, Pacing up and down) only raise Urgent if 'Aggressive behavior' or 'Disruptive behavior' is also recorded. This follows the house pattern '(and <presenting complaint> (or ...))' and matches the page's 'aggressive/disruptive patient with any of', so it is a note on behaviour, not a defect.

No system_diagnosis_rule exists, which is right: the page has no 'X likely' or 'consider X' statements. The cause labels (stimulant/alcohol withdrawal, seizures, delirium, psychosis) only select sedation and carry no criteria here; the conditions that gate sedation choice (> 65 years, substance user, previous olanzapine intolerance) and involuntary admission have no consumer because manage tasks are out of scope by design.

summary: All six red-box criteria and the Urgent priority are encoded with existing SNOMED concepts, and every check_for item is consumed by the priority rule. The one weakness is 'Feeling physically tense' for the observed sign 'tense posturing / clenching fists': a subjective-feeling concept standing in for a behaviour, with no exact SNOMED alternative. Everything below the red-box header is sedation management and flowchart routing, out of scope by design; no diagnostic logic was missed.
